nodes.name: Peat moss
nodes.desc: Moss that builds the raised bogs. Wikipedia says its slowly decaying remains accumulate as peat and its wet carpets hold many times their dry weight in water.

nodes.name: Heather
nodes.desc: Small evergreen shrub of the heath and moorland. Sheep graze it in the High Fens, and deer browse it elsewhere.

nodes.name: Bilberry
nodes.desc: Low berry shrub of the moorland. Its leaves and berries feed black grouse, deer and voles.

nodes.name: Purple moor-grass
nodes.desc: Tussock grass that spreads over drained or degraded bog. It is named as one of the problems restoration projects try to reverse.

nodes.name: Norway spruce
nodes.desc: Planted widely around the fens. The plantations are listed among the causes of damage to the bogs, but the trees feed deer and grouse.

nodes.name: Roe deer
nodes.desc: Small deer of woodland edges and moor. It browses heather, bilberry and young spruce, and is listed among the mammals of the High Fens.

nodes.name: Red deer
nodes.desc: Large deer of forest and moor that browses heather and bilberry shoots.

nodes.name: Bank vole
nodes.desc: Small rodent of heath and scrub that eats bilberry and other low plants. It is a main food of many predators.

nodes.name: European hare
nodes.desc: Grazer of grass and herbs on open ground, and prey for foxes, wildcats and birds of prey.

nodes.name: Black grouse
nodes.desc: The emblem of the nature park and endangered in the High Fens. Eats bilberry shoots and berries and, in winter, conifer needles; chicks eat insects.

nodes.name: Common green grasshopper
nodes.desc: Grassland grasshopper recorded across the plateau, feeding on grasses and eaten by frogs and birds.

nodes.name: Common frog
nodes.desc: Amphibian of wet heath and pools that eats insects and other small invertebrates. Snakes, foxes and raptors eat it.

nodes.name: Stoat
nodes.desc: Slender weasel that hunts voles, shrews, young hares and small birds.

nodes.name: Common adder
nodes.desc: Venomous snake of heath and bog edges, feeding on voles, lizards and frogs.

nodes.name: Common buzzard
nodes.desc: Common bird of prey over the plateau, taking voles, hares, frogs and snakes.

nodes.name: Red kite
nodes.desc: Raptor and frequent scavenger. It takes small mammals and frogs, and feeds on carcasses.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Generalist hunter that eats voles, hares, frogs and ground birds. Wikipedia names it among the predators of black grouse.

nodes.name: European wildcat
nodes.desc: Shy forest cat that hunts voles, hares, birds and frogs.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Summer light drives the growth of the heath and moor plants.

nodes.name: Rainfall
nodes.desc: The raised bogs are fed by rain rather than surface water, so rainfall keeps the peat wet and the moss growing.

nodes.name: Peat
nodes.desc: Waterlogged, acid ground made of slowly decaying moss. Wikipedia says the High Fens bogs are over 10,000 years old.

nodes.name: Fire
nodes.desc: Dry spells raise the fire risk on the bogs, and a large wildfire burned part of the High Fens in 2026.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals. In the acid, waterlogged bog this is very slow, so peat builds up.
